newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed market firmer on back of July CPI.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed market firmer on back of July CPI.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities prices were higher in the wake of July consumer price and industrial production data.
Discount coupons were as much as 14/32 firmer, while premium coupons were 2/32 to 3/32 higher.
Mortgage prices were up in sympathy with Treasuries, which were were bolstered by the morning data that appeared to suggest that inflation was at bay.
As reported, July consumer prices were up 0.2 percent. The so-called core rate also rose 0.2 percent. July industrial output rose 0.2 percent, while capacity fell to 83.1 percent.
A pass-through trader said that while mortgage-backed prices rose early, activity appeared to "be very subdued." There were some small lists of inverse floaters out for bid, the trader said.
He called the increase in the Mortgage Bankers Association of America refinance index "no surprise."
As reported, the MBA refinancing index rose 4.3 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis to 718.8 in the week ended August 8, compared with the prior week's 689.3.
While MBA said the refinancing index has peaked, the trader contended that refis will not necessarily fall off.
